questions.q: She was exhausted because she ___ for three hours.
questions.explanation: Use the past perfect continuous for an action in progress before another past moment.

questions.q: By the time the doctor arrived, the patient ___ for half an hour.
questions.explanation: Use the past perfect continuous to stress duration before a past point.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: They have been living in Madrid since 2015 before they moved.
They were living in Madrid since 2015 before they moved.
They had been lived in Madrid since 2015 before they moved.
They had been living in Madrid since 2015 before they moved.
questions.explanation: 'Since 2015' with a past reference point needs the past perfect continuous.

questions.q: He couldn't concentrate because he ___ all night.
questions.explanation: Use the past perfect continuous for the cause of a past situation.

questions.q: When I saw them, they ___ about the trip.
questions.explanation: Use the past perfect continuous for an activity already in progress at a past moment.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I had been study all day when you called.
I have been studying all day when you called.
I was studying all day when you called.
I had been studying all day when you called.
questions.explanation: After 'had been', use the -ing form of the verb.

questions.q: The roads were wet because it ___ since morning.
questions.explanation: Use the past perfect continuous with 'since' for duration before a past moment.

questions.q: She ___ English for two years before she passed the exam.
questions.explanation: Use the past perfect continuous for a long activity leading up to a past event.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: We have been waiting for an hour when the bus finally arrived.
We were waiting for an hour when the bus finally arrived.
We had waited for an hour when the bus finally arrived.
We had been waiting for an hour when the bus finally arrived.
questions.explanation: Only the past perfect continuous stresses that the waiting was still in progress.

questions.q: By 2010, they ___ the company for a decade.
questions.explanation: With 'by 2010' and a duration, use the past perfect continuous.

questions.q: My eyes were red because I ___ all evening.
questions.explanation: Use the past perfect continuous to explain a visible past result.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: She had been saving money for years before buying the house.
She has been saving money for years before buying the house.
She was saving money for years before buying the house.
She had been saved money for years before buying the house.
questions.explanation: A finished past period of saving needs the past perfect continuous.

questions.q: They ___ football when it started to rain.
questions.explanation: Use the past perfect continuous for an activity interrupted by another past event.

questions.q: When she got home, her brother ___ on the sofa for hours.
questions.explanation: Use the past perfect continuous for duration before a past arrival.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: He has been working there for ten years before he was promoted.
He had been working there for ten years before he was promoted.
He worked there for ten years before he was promoted.
He had been worked there for ten years before he was promoted.
questions.explanation: Duration before a past promotion needs the past perfect continuous.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: They have been arguing since morning when I arrived.
They argued since morning when I arrived.
They had been argued since morning when I arrived.
They had been arguing since morning when I arrived.
questions.explanation: 'Since morning' before a past arrival needs the past perfect continuous.

questions.q: She was angry because her neighbour ___ loud music all night.
questions.explanation: Use the past perfect continuous for the ongoing cause of a past feeling.

questions.q: By the time the show started, we ___ in line for an hour.
questions.explanation: Use the past perfect continuous for waiting that lasted until a past moment.

questions.q: He looked ill because he ___ well for weeks.
questions.explanation: The negative past perfect continuous stresses a long period without the action.

questions.q: We ___ each other for years before we met in person.
questions.explanation: Use the past perfect continuous for repeated contact leading up to a past meeting.
